# Every open engine issue gets a premise read and a verdict

## Context

The operator, 2026-11-05: *"We resolve 200+ tickets every week, yet inside engine and brain repos we have backlog items that are several months old and rot. We need to check if intents are still valid, even in case the code reality can have changed a lot. The benefit is getting to a clean slate which betters allows us planning new items afterwards."*

**Measured 2026-11-05 10:20Z:** 189 open; 111 filed more than 180 days ago; 94 unassigned; 102 authored by the operator. No engine ticket older than a month was completed in the 30 days before 11-02 (Vega's flow read, comment 6584643052).

This body replaces the July framing (v13.2 milestone, 163 tickets), which is in the edit history. The tranche ledgers in the comments stay as history. The Brain half is neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1438, and this body copies its shape.

## The rules (operator, 2026-10-17, binding; comment 6244102341)

- Age is not a staleness signal. Read by **domain**, by the peer who knows that code. The assignee is a hint, never the reader of first resort.
- Each verdict starts with a premise check against current source (file:line, PR or ADR), then ends one of four ways:
  - **close**, with the resolving or superseding citation;
  - **rewrite** the body to the current architecture;
  - **convert to a Discussion**, when it is a valid idea with no plan;
  - **holds**: premise verified and body current; a dated premise-read comment counts as checked.
- **Bugs get fixed, not triaged.** The count is an outcome, never the target. No bulk close by age.
- **An operator-authored ticket (op) is the operator's call.** The reader posts the verdict as a comment, and he closes it.
- The contributor set stays open for contributors.

## The instrument

- This body. **Verdicts live on the tickets themselves**, never as comments here.
- Claim a domain (or part of one) with one comment. The claimer ticks a box once its ticket carries the verdict, and marks each operator-pending verdict in its line.
- Tags: `op` = operator-authored; other names are assignees (hints); `PR #N open` = in flight, ticks on merge.

## Tranche: landed-work candidates — 17 examined, 1 resolved, and the heuristic's false-positive rate is the finding

Joining @neo-fable-clio's lane rather than replacing it — both seats stand, and hers takes precedence on return. This has not moved since 2026-07-10 while being, almost word for word, what the operator asked for this morning: *reduce the backlog by resolving existing tickets, and avoid opening new ones.*

**Scale check first, because the ticket's premise has aged.** Filed against **233 open / 163 invisible**. Live count today: **144 open**. The set shrank by 89 without this sweep running, so the tranches below are against a different, smaller population than the body describes.

### The tranche's selector

Not domain-first, as the body proposes — **resolution-first**, because it is the one class of triage that costs **zero review budget**, and review budget is today's binding constraint (one shared GPT rate limit, nearly spent). An already-finished ticket closes on evidence alone.

```
git log --oneline --grep "(#N)" origin/dev   # for each open N
```

17 of 144 open tickets have a commit on `dev` naming them.

### Verdicts

| # | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **#18145** | **resolved → closing** | all four ACs met; every batch landed, AC-4's guard shipped in neomjs/neo#18196 with its own CI workflow. Measured 0 files pending against the 26 files / 62 blocks it was filed on. Closes via PR neomjs/neo#18725 (approved, CLEAN). |
| neomjs/neo#16498 | stays open | **false positive.** PR neomjs/neo#16719 resolves neomjs/neo#16718 and only `Refs neomjs/neo#16498`; its body says so. Verified the plain/film arms green at head; the one red is neomjs/neo#16756's, environment-bound. |
| neomjs/neo#9849 | stays open | post + index + links met; **AC-3 is blocked by a defect outside it** — `sitemap.xml` serves 1,016 URLs and zero blog routes, for every post. AC-4 is a publication act no agent performs. |
| neomjs/neo#17175 | stays open | 8 ACs, the landed commit covers a subset. |
| neomjs/neo#17171 | stays open | 6 ACs, all requiring live-ruleset verification. |
| neomjs/neo#15614 | stays open | AC-4 wants `DemoBWorkspace.mjs` ≤ 1500 lines; it is **4,430**. |
| neomjs/github-content-sync#26 | stays open | `[PROVISIONAL_UNGRADUATED]`, pre-quorum, explicitly not implementation-authorizing. The landed commit's close target was neomjs/neo#18449. |
| neomjs/neo-agent-institution#889 · neomjs/neo#15252 · neomjs/neo#15243 · neomjs/neo-agent-skills#299 · neomjs/neo#16151 | stay open | no checked ACs; neomjs/neo#15252 is an epic, so its ACs live in subs. |
| neomjs/neo#9404 · neomjs/neo#9486 · neomjs/neo#9492 | stay open | epics; a commit naming an epic is expected and means nothing about closure. |

### The reusable half — the heuristic over-reports, and here is why

**A commit subject naming a ticket is not evidence that ticket closed.** neomjs/neo#16498 is the specimen: the subject reads `(#16498) (#16719)`, the split happened mid-flight, and the subject kept the pre-split number while the PR body carried the real close target. Subjects are written before dispositions settle.

So this selector is a **candidate generator, never a verdict** — 1 hit in 17. Anyone running it must read each candidate's ACs against reality; skipping that is how a premature closure happens, which is the failure neomjs/neo#18208 was reopened for.

### Second finding: ten aged tickets are stranded, not stale

Assignment, not age, is what makes these invisible — they look owned and cannot move:

| assignee | open | state |
|---|---:|---|
| `neo-fable-clio` | 5 | dark |
| `neo-gpt` | 4 | offline |
| `neo-fable` | 1 | dark |

`#18303` · `#17783` · `#16742` · `#15520` · `#15252` · `#15243` · `#15000` · `#14230` · `#13158` · `#12964`.

I am **not** unassigning anyone — a dark peer cannot object, and the claim is theirs. Listing them so they become self-selectable is the whole intervention. An unassigned aged ticket at least reads as available; an aged ticket assigned to an unreachable seat reads as covered, which is worse than invisible. That distinction is missing from this ticket's classification, and I think it belongs in it: **stranded** is a fourth verdict beside v13.2-relevant, valid-but-later, and resolved.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-10-18T01:13:33Z

**Direction for the next tranche, from the operator (2026-10-17, ~23:30 Berlin).** The release after 13.3 may be dedicated to the backlog: 240 open issues on `neomjs/neo`, with a goal of about 100.

His two corrections to my first framing are binding for this sweep:
1. **Age is not a staleness signal.** "Even tickets that are just 2 weeks old might no longer reflect the current reality." So the sweep covers every open ticket, ordered by domain, each read by the peer who knows that code. It is not ordered oldest-first.
2. **No closing without proper investigation.** The count is an outcome, never the target.

Each verdict carries a premise check against current source (file:line, PR or ADR), and ends one of three ways:
- **close** with a citation, when it was resolved or superseded;
- **rewrite** the body to the current architecture, when the idea holds but the text is stale;
- **convert to a Discussion**, when it's a valid idea with no plan.

The good-first / Hacktoberfest set stays open for contributors. Bugs get fixed, not triaged. New tickets are fine when they replace or bundle old ones.
